knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates the transcriptional regulation of MIR196A by estrogen and its role as a prognostic biomarker in ER+ breast cancer. MIR196A is transcribed from two distinct genomic loci and targets genes involved in apoptosis, angiogenesis, and cell cycle progression. The research demonstrates that MIR196A expression is dynamically controlled by long-range interactions between ERα-bound enhancers and promoters.

knowledge_units.context_summary: MIR196A directly targets p27/Kip1 to influence the cell cycle and promote oncogenic features in cancer cell lines. The transcriptional regulation of miRNA genes, including MIR196A, involves promoters with specific histone marks and enhancer elements. In breast cancer, MIR196A expression correlates with HOXC genes and is regulated by oestrogen, as demonstrated by RNA polymerase II binding in MCF7 cells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: MIR196A expression patterns in breast cancer correlate with hormone receptor status and PAM50 subtypes, with high expression linked to poor survival in ER+ disease but better outcomes in triple-negative breast cancer. The gene serves as a prognostic biomarker where high expression predicts poor survival in post-menopausal ER+ patients but good survival in premenopausal patients. DNA methylation of the upstream CpG island is high in cancerous and non-malignant cell lines but low in normal mammary epithelial cells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: MIR196A expression varies significantly across different breast cancer resistance models, increasing in tamoxifen and chemotherapy resistance but decreasing in fulvestrant resistance. These expression changes correlate with DNA methylation patterns at the HOXC10/MIR196A2 promoters and increased ERα binding in resistant tumors. The discussion links these regulatory mechanisms to the role of ERα and cofactors in maintaining active transcription and low methylation levels.

The passage also details the cell culture and cloning methods used to study MIR196A regulation.
